title: The order server on your router

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the order server starts on your router and answers real requests.

tasks.title: Group routes under a prefix
tasks.description:
Implement `mount(router, prefix, group)` in `src/router.js`, where `group` is another router made by `createRouter()`.

- every route of the group answers at the prefix followed by its own path: with `mount(router, '/staff', staff)`, staff's `GET /queue` answers `GET /staff/queue`, and staff's `/` answers `/staff` itself
- the group's routes do not answer at their own paths, and a path is in the group only when its first parts are exactly the prefix: `/staffroom` is not under `/staff`
- the group's middleware runs after the router's own, and only for the group's routes
- errors from the group's routes go to the router's error handler
- group routes take part in 404, 405 and choosing between routes like any other route
- it throws a `TypeError` when `prefix` is not a string that starts with `/`

A group is mounted once its routes and middleware are added. The check builds routers and groups of its own and sends requests through `handle`.
nextSteps: Read the comment above `mount` and decide where a group's routes end up.
Give each of the group's routes its full path: the prefix, then its own path.
Make each such route remember the group's middleware.
In `handle`, run the router's middleware, then the route's group middleware, then the handler.
hints: The rest of the router already knows how to match, choose, say 404 and 405, and handle errors. If a group's routes simply become routes of the router with longer paths, all of that works for them too.
Each route needs to carry its group's middleware with it, so `handle` can put that middleware into the chain for that route only. Keep a reference to the group's list, not a copy.
In `mount`: `router.routes.push({ ...route, path: prefix + route.path, groups: [group.middleware] })`, with `/` mapped to the prefix. In `handle`: `[router.middleware, ...route.groups].flat()`.

tasks.title: Serve real requests
tasks.description:
Implement `serve(router)` in `src/router.js`, and teach `handle` the `HEAD` method.

- `serve` returns a server made with `createServer` from `node:http`, not listening yet: whoever calls it chooses where it listens
- the server sends every request through `handle(router, req, res)`
- when `handle` throws or rejects and nothing was answered yet, the client gets a plain `500` with `{ error }`, and the server goes on to answer the next request
- a `HEAD` request is answered by the path's `HEAD` route, or when it has none, by its `GET` route; Node leaves the body out by itself

The check starts your server on a port the system picks, sends it real requests with queries, bodies and methods of its own, and closes it.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and read the error.
Make the server in `serve` with a listener that calls `handle`.
Catch what `handle` throws or rejects with, and answer 500 if nothing was sent.
Look at the `HEAD /prices` line, and let `handle` fall back to the GET route.
hints: A real request is the same shape as the ones your router has met all along: a stream with `method`, `url` and `headers`, and a response with `statusCode`, `setHeader` and `end`. Nothing in the router has to change for it.
The listener can be an `async` function. `await handle(...)` inside a `try` turns both a throw and a rejection into something your `catch` sees; `res.headersSent` says whether an answer has started.

`return createServer(async (req, res) => { try { await handle(router, req, res) } catch { if (!res.headersSent) sendJson(res, 500, { error: ... }) } })`. For HEAD, look for GET routes when no HEAD route fits.

tasks.title: Move the order server onto your router
tasks.description:
Implement `createApp(shop, { staffKey })` in `src/app.js`. It returns a router that answers every request of the order page, as the comment in the file lists:

- `GET /prices`, `GET /orders` (filtered by `status`, and by one or more `item` in the query), `GET /orders/today`, `GET /orders/:id` (404 with `{ error }` for an order that does not exist) and `POST /orders` (201 with the new order)
- a group under `/staff`, whose middleware answers `401` with `{ error }` unless the `x-staff-key` header is `staffKey`, with `GET /staff/queue` and `POST /staff/orders/:id/status`
- one error handler: a `ShopError` is answered with its own status and `{ error: its message }`, anything else with a plain 500

Every other request gets the answer your router gives by itself: a wrong method is a 405, an unknown path a 404. The check runs your app on a server of its own, with orders of its own, and sends it the order page's requests and the ones the old server got wrong.
nextSteps: Open `src/old-server.js` and `src/shop.js`: every branch of the old chain becomes a route.
Add the public routes and the error handler first, and run `node src/try.js`.
Make a second router for staff, give it its middleware and routes, and mount it at `/staff`.
Let handlers throw a `ShopError` instead of answering errors themselves.
hints: Each handler is one or two lines: read what the request carries (`req.params`, `req.query`, `req.body`), ask the shop, answer with `sendJson`.
`req.query.item` is a string when it comes once and an array when it comes more than once. `[req.query.item ?? []].flat()` is always an array.
`const staff = createRouter()`, then `use(staff, (req, res, next) => ...)`, then its routes, and only then `mount(app, '/staff', staff)`.
